description: Experience the ultimate crunch with these crispy potato samosas, a quintessential Indian appetizer loved by all. Each golden, flaky pastry encases a perfectly spiced potato and pea filling, offering a burst of authentic flavors. Ideal for tea time snacks or festive gatherings, these homemade samosas are sure to impress your guests.

ingredients.notes: for dough, plus more for frying

instructions.title: Prepare the Samosa Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, salt, and carom seeds if using. Add 1/4 cup of ghee or oil and rub it into the flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Gradually add water, a little at a time, and knead to form a firm, smooth dough. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Potato Filling
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped ginger and green chilies, and saute for 1 minute. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, then add the green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Combine Filling Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the coarsely mashed potatoes to the pan with the spices and peas. Mix well, ensuring all ingredients are evenly combined. Add dry mango powder and fresh coriander leaves. Season with salt to taste. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat and let the filling cool completely.

instructions.title: Shape the Samosa Pastry
instructions.text: Divide the rested dough into equal small balls, about the size of a golf ball. Roll each ball into an oval shape, about 6-7 inches long and 4 inches wide. Cut the oval in half lengthwise to create two semi-circles. This will give you two samosa bases from each rolled piece.

instructions.title: Fill and Seal the Samosas
instructions.text: Take one semi-circle, wet the straight edge lightly with water. Bring the two ends of the straight edge together to form a cone shape, pressing firmly to seal. Fill the cone with 1-2 tablespoons of the cooled potato filling. Wet the top inner edges of the cone and press them together to seal the samosa, creating a triangular or pyramidal shape. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

instructions.title: Deep Fry the Samosas
instructions.text: Heat oil for deep frying in a kadai or deep pan over medium-low heat. The oil should not be too hot, as this will prevent the pastry from becoming crispy. Gently slide the shaped samosas into the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding. Fry them on low to medium heat, turning occasionally, until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 10-12 minutes per batch. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels.

instructions.title: Serve Crispy Samosas
instructions.text: Serve the hot, crispy potato samosas immediately with your favorite chutney, such as mint chutney or tamarind chutney, or with a cup of hot chai. Enjoy this classic Indian appetizer!

tips: For perfectly crispy samosas, knead a firm dough and ensure the oil is not too hot when frying. Frying on medium-low heat allows the pastry to cook through and become flaky.
Do not overfill the samosas, as this can cause them to burst during frying. A good seal is crucial for maintaining their shape and crispness.

Samosas can be prepared ahead of time and frozen before frying. Freeze them on a tray until solid, then transfer to an airtight container. Fry from frozen, adding a few extra minutes to the cooking time.
